plans.rationale: This is the first round of investigation for INC-03. We need to establish the exact symptom onset and error patterns for payments-api and mobile-bff using observability, while simultaneously checking all recent dependency changes, deploys, and the service dependency graph around these services and external payment components like upi-gateway and npci-switch.

tasks.goal: Establish symptom onset, error rates, and p99 latency for payments-api and mobile-bff, and check downstream calls to upi-gateway.
Review recent deploys, config changes, and feature flags across all services, and map the dependency graph around payments-api, mobile-bff, upi-gateway, and external payment providers.
Establish symptom onset, error rates, and p99 latency for payments-api and mobile-bff, and check downstream calls to upi-gateway.
Review recent deploys, config changes, and feature flags across all services, and map the dependency graph around payments-api, mobile-bff, upi-gateway, and external payment providers.
Build and rank competing root-cause hypotheses

r1-dependency-2.summary: Mapped dependency chains and reviewed deployments, configuration changes, and feature flags across all services in the 7 days prior to the incident. Identified relevant changes prior to the incident onset at 13:45 UTC, including a fraud-service rules change at 13:30 UTC and ledger-service and orders-service deploys earlier that day.

findings.statement: payments-api synchronously calls ledger-service, upi-gateway, fraud-service, and redis-cache, and asynchronously calls event-bus.
upi-gateway synchronously calls npci-switch and partner-bank-api.
fraud-service configuration was modified at 2026-10-04T13:30:00+00:00 to raise velocity threshold from 5 to 7 transactions/min.
ledger-service was deployed at 2026-10-04T12:29:00+00:00 with v6.7.0 routine release.
orders-service was deployed at 2026-10-04T12:07:00+00:00 with v1.25.0 routine release.

open_questions: Did the fraud-service rules change or ledger-service deploy contribute to latencies in payments-api?
How is npci-switch behaving during the time of the incident since logs are absent for external services?

r1-observability-1.summary: Observability data for INC-03 shows that symptom onsets begin around 13:43 to 13:47 UTC on 2026-10-04. upi-gateway latency p99 spiked first at 13:43 UTC followed by payments-api p99 latency jump at 13:45 UTC, and error rates spiking across payments-api, mobile-bff, and upi-gateway around 13:46-13:47 UTC. The root cause traces further upstream to partner-bank-api latency spikes starting at 13:41 UTC, leading to worker exhaustion at upi-gateway and subsequent timeouts in payments-api.

findings.statement: upi-gateway latency p99 anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:43:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 10665.76ms.
upi-gateway error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:46:00+00:00, peaking at 13.72%.
payments-api latency p99 anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:45:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 10772.92ms.
payments-api error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:47:00+00:00, peaking at 12.58%.
payments-api CPU usage anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:46:00+00:00, reaching a peak of 57.2%.
payments-api logged repeated timeout errors calling upi-gateway POST /v2/collect after 10000ms.
mobile-bff error rate anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:47:00+00:00, peaking at 4.67%.
upi-gateway logged worker pool exhaustion rejecting requests due to being busy waiting on partner-bank-api.
partner-bank-api latency p99 anomaly started at 2026-10-04T13:41:00+00:00, peaking at 9237.07ms.

open_questions: What specific change or internal failure occurred within partner-bank-api at 13:41 UTC to trigger the latency spike?

hypotheses.title: Partner Bank API Latency Spike Causing Worker Exhaustion
hypotheses.mechanism: partner-bank-api latency increased starting at 13:41 UTC, causing upi-gateway calls to block and exhaust its worker pool by 13:47 UTC. This in turn caused requests from payments-api to time out after 10000ms, triggering error rate and latency spikes in payments-api and mobile-bff.

supporting.note: Shows partner-bank-api latency spike beginning at 13:41 UTC, which precedes all other dependent service anomalies.
Shows upi-gateway latency anomaly starting at 13:43 UTC, directly following the partner bank latency increase.
Confirms upi-gateway workers were exhausted because they were waiting on partner-bank-api.
Shows payments-api timing out when calling upi-gateway.
Shows payments-api latency p99 anomaly starting at 13:45 UTC.

assumptions: The underlying cause of the partner-bank-api latency is an external issue at the partner bank.

hypotheses.title: Fraud Service Configuration Change Induced Processing Delays
hypotheses.mechanism: A change to fraud rules raising the velocity threshold at 13:30 UTC altered traffic patterns or checks, leading to downstream processing contention.

supporting.note: Configuration change on fraud-service occurred shortly before the incident onset.

contradicting.note: Latency started rising at 13:41 UTC, whereas logs specifically show workers waiting on partner-bank-api rather than fraud-service.
Worker pool exhaustion is explicitly attributed to waiting on partner-bank-api, not fraud-service.

assumptions: The fraud-service velocity threshold change indirectly caused downstream banking provider delays.

hypotheses.reasoning_summary: The incident onset is established at 2026-10-04T13:41:00+00:00 by the partner-bank-api latency anomaly metric. The telemetry clearly points to a cascading failure where upstream partner-bank-api slowness exhausted upi-gateway worker pools, leading to timeout errors in payments-api. Hypothesis H1 is well-supported by timing and direct worker exhaustion logs, whereas H2 (fraud-service config change) lacks direct supporting telemetry connecting it to partner bank latency.

adjustments.reason: Direct telemetry proves partner-bank-api latency spike started at 13:41 UTC, perfectly preceding upi-gateway worker exhaustion and payments-api timeouts. The alternative hypothesis H2 is contradicted by direct log evidence showing workers waiting on partner-bank-api rather than fraud-service.
Contradicted by direct log evidence attributing worker exhaustion to partner-bank-api, and preceded by no supporting telemetry linking fraud-service config changes to partner bank latency.
